bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷六十四 唐書40: 列傳16 霍彥威 王晏球 戴思遠 朱漢賓 孔勍 劉玘 周知裕
title.en: Volume 64 Book of Later Tang 40: Biographies 16 - Hou Yanwei, Wang Yanqiu, Dai Siyuan, Zhu Hanbin, Kong Qing, Liu Qi, Zhou Zhiyu
title.raw: 卷六十四 唐書40: 列傳16 霍彥威 王晏球 戴思遠 朱漢賓 孔勍 劉玘 周知裕 Volume 64 Book of Later Tang 40: Biographies 16 - Hou Yanwei, Wang Yanqiu, Dai Siyuan, Zhu Hanbin, Kong Qing, Liu Qi, Zhou Zhiyu

sentences.zh: 霍彥威，字子重，洺州曲周人也。

translations.literal: Huo Yanwei, whose courtesy name was Zizhong, was a native of Quzhou in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei, courtesy name Zizhong, came from Quzhou in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁將霍存得之於村落間，年十四，從征討。

translations.literal: The Liang general Huo Cun obtained him in a village; he was fourteen and followed on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Huo Cun found him in the countryside when he was fourteen, and the boy followed him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 存憐其爽邁，養為己子。

translations.literal: Cun pitied his bold and open manner and raised him as his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Cun took a liking to his spirited bearing and adopted him as his son.

sentences.zh: 存，梁史有傳。

translations.literal: Cun has a biography in the Liang history.
translations.idiomatic: Cun has a biography in the history of Liang.

sentences.zh: 彥威未弱冠，為梁祖所知，擢在左右，漸升戎秩，亟立戰功。

translations.literal: Before Yanwei had reached twenty, the Liang Founder took notice of him, promoted him to his side, and he gradually rose in military rank, repeatedly earning battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yanwei came of age, the Liang Founder noticed him and kept him at his side; he rose steadily through the ranks and won distinction again and again in battle.

sentences.zh: 嘗中流矢，眇其一目。

translations.literal: He once was struck by a stray arrow and lost sight in one eye.
translations.idiomatic: He was once hit by a stray arrow and lost the use of one eye.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，自開封府押衙、右親從指揮使、檢校司空授右龍驤軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping, from Kaifeng Prefecture Escort Officer, Right Close Attendant Commander, and Acting Minister of Works he was appointed Right Dragon-Tiger Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiping he was made commander of the Right Dragon-Tiger Army, having served as Kaifeng escort officer, commander of the right close attendants, and acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年，自右監門衛將軍授左天武軍使，遷右監門上將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, from Right Gate Guard General he was appointed Left Heavenly Martial Army Commander and was transferred to Right Gate Guard Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he moved from Right Gate Guard general to commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Army, then was promoted to senior general of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 乾化三年，與袁象先同誅朱友珪，梁末帝授洺州刺史，轉河陽留後。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianhua, together with Yuan Xiangxian he killed Zhu Yougui; the Last Liang Emperor appointed him prefect of Ming Prefecture and then transferred him to regent of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianhua he joined Yuan Xiangxian in killing Zhu Yougui; the Last Liang Emperor made him prefect of Ming, then regent of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 乾化末，邠州留後李保衡背李茂貞以城歸梁，梁以彥威為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianhua, Binzhou regent Li Baoheng turned from Li Maozhen and surrendered the city to Liang; Liang made Yanwei military governor of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianhua, Li Baoheng, regent of Bin, broke with Li Maozhen and surrendered the city to Liang, which appointed Yanwei military governor of Bin.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，茂貞遣將劉知俊率大軍攻之，彥威固守逾年，竟不能下；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, Maozhen sent the general Liu Zhijun at the head of a great army to attack; Yanwei held firm for more than a year, and in the end they could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: That May, Maozhen sent General Liu Zhijun with a large army to attack, but Yanwei held out for more than a year and the city could not be taken;

sentences.zh: 或得其俘，悉令放之，秦人懷其惠，遂無侵擾。

translations.literal: Whenever he captured prisoners, he ordered them all released; the people of Qin remembered his kindness, and thereafter there was no harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took prisoners he set them all free; the people of Qin were grateful for his kindness, and raids ceased.

sentences.zh: 轉滑州節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Hua.

sentences.zh: 移鎮鄆州，兼北面行營招討，總大軍於河上。

translations.literal: He was moved to garrison Yan and concurrently made northern campaign pacification commissioner, commanding the great army on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Yan and made northern campaign pacification commissioner, taking overall command of the army on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 師徒屢敗，降授陝州留後。

translations.literal: His army suffered repeated defeats, and he was demoted and appointed regent of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats he was demoted to regent of Shan.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，彥威自陝馳至請罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yanwei galloped from Shan to submit himself and beg forgiveness; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yanwei rode in from Shan to surrender and beg pardon, and an edict absolved him.

sentences.zh: 一日，莊宗於崇元殿宴諸將，彥威與段凝、袁象先等預會。

translations.literal: One day Emperor Zhuangzong held a banquet for the generals in the Chongyuan Hall; Yanwei, together with Duan Ning, Yuan Xiangxian, and others, was present.
translations.idiomatic: One day Emperor Zhuangzong entertained his generals in the Chongyuan Hall; Yanwei was there with Duan Ning, Yuan Xiangxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，莊宗舉酒屬明宗曰：「 此席宴客，皆吾前歲之勁敵也，一旦與吾同宴，蓋卿前鋒之效也。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Emperor Zhuangzong raised his cup and addressed Emperor Mingzong, saying: "The guests at this banquet were all my fierce enemies of recent years; that they now feast with me at once is surely the effect of your vanguard work.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Emperor Zhuangzong raised his cup to Emperor Mingzong and said, "Every guest at this table was a formidable enemy of mine only a year ago. That they now sit and feast with me is surely thanks to your work on the front lines.

sentences.zh: 」彥威等伏陛謝罪，莊宗曰：「與卿話舊，無足畏也。

translations.literal: " Yanwei and the others prostrated themselves on the steps to beg forgiveness; Emperor Zhuangzong said: "I am merely reminiscing with you; there is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanwei and the others prostrated themselves on the steps to beg forgiveness. Emperor Zhuangzong said, "We are only talking over old times; there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」 因賜禦衣、器幣，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: " He then bestowed imperial robes and ritual gifts, and they drank their fill before the banquet ended.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gave them imperial robes and gifts, and they drank until all were satisfied before the feast broke up.

sentences.zh: 尋放歸藩。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was allowed to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was permitted to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 明年，從明宗平潞州，授徐州節度使。

translations.literal: The next year, following Emperor Mingzong in pacifying Luzhou, he was appointed military governor of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed Emperor Mingzong in pacifying Luzhou and was made military governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯塞，莊宗以明宗為北面招討使，命彥威為副。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier, Emperor Zhuangzong made Emperor Mingzong northern pacification commissioner and ordered Yanwei as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border, Emperor Zhuangzong appointed Emperor Mingzong northern pacification commissioner and made Yanwei his deputy.

sentences.zh: 彥威善言論，頗能接奉，明宗尤重之。

translations.literal: Yanwei was skilled in discourse and quite able in attending and serving; Emperor Mingzong especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was an engaging speaker and knew how to win people over; Emperor Mingzong held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 趙太叛於邢州，奉詔討平之。

translations.literal: Zhao Tai rebelled at Xing Prefecture; by imperial order he was sent to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Tai rebelled at Xing, he received orders to put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 時趙在禮據魏州，與明宗會兵於鄴下，大軍夕亂，明宗為其所逼，彥威從入魏州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Zaili held Wei Prefecture; he joined forces with Emperor Mingzong below Ye, and at evening the great army fell into disorder; Emperor Mingzong was pressed by them, and Yanwei followed him into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zaili then held Wei; he and Emperor Mingzong joined forces below Ye, but at nightfall the army mutinied and forced Emperor Mingzong in, with Yanwei following him into the city.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉等尤忌彥威，欲殺之，彥威機辯開說，竟免。

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui and the others especially resented Yanwei and wished to kill him; Yanwei, quick-witted and eloquent, argued and persuaded them, and in the end he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui and his men especially hated Yanwei and wanted him dead, but Yanwei talked his way out of it with quick wit and was spared.

sentences.zh: 及出，彥威部下兵士獨全，衛護明宗至魏縣。

translations.literal: When they came out, only Yanwei's troops remained intact; they escorted Emperor Mingzong as far as Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: When they left the city, Yanwei alone kept his troops intact and escorted Emperor Mingzong to Wei County.

sentences.zh: 時明宗欲北趨常山，彥威與安重誨懇請赴闕。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Mingzong wished to hurry north toward Changshan; Yanwei and An Chonghui earnestly urged him to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong then wanted to flee north toward Changshan, but Yanwei and An Chonghui urgently persuaded him to go to the capital instead.

sentences.zh: 從至洛陽，彥威首率卿相勸進於至德宮。

translations.literal: He followed to Luoyang, and Yanwei was the first to lead the ministers and grandees in urging accession at the Zhide Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He followed to Luoyang, where Yanwei was first among the ministers to urge his accession at the Zhide Palace.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，內外機事，皆決於彥威。

translations.literal: Within ten days, all internal and external affairs of state were decided by Yanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days every matter of state, at home and abroad, was decided by Yanwei.

sentences.zh: 擅收段凝、溫韜下獄，將置於法。

translations.literal: On his own authority he seized Duan Ning and Wen Tao and put them in prison, intending to punish them by law.
translations.idiomatic: He took it upon himself to arrest Duan Ning and Wen Tao and throw them in prison, intending to have them executed.

sentences.zh: 安重誨曰：「溫、段罪惡，負於梁室，眾所知矣。

translations.literal: An Chonghui said: "Wen and Duan are guilty and have wronged the house of Liang; this is known to all.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui said, "Wen and Duan are guilty men who betrayed the house of Liang, as everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 今主上克平內艱，冀安萬國，豈為公報仇耶！

translations.literal: Now our lord has overcome internal troubles and hopes to settle the realm; would he settle your private score of vengeance!
translations.idiomatic: Our lord has just overcome internal crisis and hopes to bring peace to the realm. Surely he is not settling your private score!

sentences.zh: 」至天成初，除鄆州節度使。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed military governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " At the start of Tiancheng he was made military governor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 值青州王公儼拒命，改平盧軍節度，至鎮，擒公儼，斬之。

translations.literal: When Wang Gongyan of Qing Prefecture defied orders, he was changed to military governor of the Pinglu Army; upon reaching his post he captured Gongyan and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gongyan of Qing defied orders, he was reassigned as military governor of Pinglu; on reaching his post he captured Gongyan and executed him.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，賜覲於汴州，明宗接遇甚厚，累官至檢校太尉、兼中書令。

translations.literal: The next winter he was granted an audience at Bian; Emperor Mingzong received him with great favor, and he rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was granted an audience at Bian, where Emperor Mingzong received him with great warmth; he rose to acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，卒於理所，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the third winter he died at his headquarters, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third winter he died at his headquarters, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 奏至之日，明宗方出近郊。

translations.literal: On the day the memorial arrived, Emperor Mingzong had just gone out to the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Mingzong was away on an outing in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 忽聞奏訃，掩泣歸宮，輟朝三日，至月終不舉樂。

translations.literal: Suddenly hearing the memorial of death, he covered his face and wept as he returned to the palace; he suspended court for three days and until the month's end did not hold music.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the news of his death he wept and returned to the palace, suspended court for three days, and forbade music for the rest of the month.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：天成四年六月敕：「故平盧軍節度使霍彥威，勳名顯著，宅兆已營，度遵定諡之規，俾議送終之制，宜以三公禮葬。」）〉

translations.literal: (Institutional History of the Five Dynasties: An edict of the sixth month of the fourth year of Tiancheng: "The late military governor of the Pinglu Army, Huo Yanwei, whose merit and fame were outstanding, has already had his tomb prepared; in accordance with the regulations for fixing posthumous titles, let the rites for seeing him to the end be discussed; he should be buried with the rites due a Three Dukes.")]
translations.idiomatic: (Institutional History of the Five Dynasties: An edict of the sixth month of the fourth year of Tiancheng: "The late military governor of Pinglu, Huo Yanwei, whose merit and fame were outstanding, already has his tomb prepared. In keeping with the regulations for fixing posthumous titles, let the rites for his funeral be determined; he should be buried with the honors due a Three Dukes.")]

sentences.zh: 冊贈太師、晉國公，諡曰忠武。

translations.literal: By patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Jin, with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Jin, with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 子承訓，弟彥珂，累曆刺史。

translations.literal: His son Chengxun and his younger brother Yanke both served in succession as prefects.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengxun and his younger brother Yanke both served terms as prefect.

sentences.zh: 皇朝乾德中，立明宗廟於洛州，詔以彥威配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era of the Imperial Dynasty, when Emperor Mingzong's temple was established at Luo Prefecture, an edict ordered Yanwei to share in the offerings in the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiande era of our dynasty, when Emperor Mingzong's temple was established at Luo, an edict made Yanwei a co-honoree in the temple rites.

sentences.zh: 王晏球，字瑩之，自言洛都人。

translations.literal: Wang Yanqiu, whose courtesy name was Yingzhi, said of himself that he was a man of the Luoyang capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqiu, courtesy name Yingzhi, claimed Luoyang as his home.

sentences.zh: 少遇亂，為蔡賊所掠，汴人杜氏畜之為子，因冒姓杜氏。

translations.literal: In youth he met with disorder and was seized by Cai bandits; a man of Bian named Du took him in as a son, and he therefore falsely took the surname Du.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was caught up in the chaos and seized by Cai bandits; a Bian man surnamed Du adopted him, and he took the Du surname.

sentences.zh: 晏球少沉勇有斷，倜儻不群。

translations.literal: Yanqiu in youth was deep, brave, and decisive, free-spirited and standing apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yanqiu was steady, brave, and decisive, with a bold and unconventional bearing.

sentences.zh: 梁祖之鎮汴也，選富家子有材力者，置之帳下，號曰「廳子都」。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder held Bian as his base, he selected sons of wealthy families with talent and strength, placed them under his command, and called them the "Hall Sons Corps."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder held Bian, he picked strong and capable sons of wealthy families for his personal retinue and called them the "Hall Sons Corps."

sentences.zh: （《清異錄》：宣武廳子都，尤勇悍，其弩張一大機，則十二小機皆發，用連珠大箭，無遠不及，晉人極畏此。）〉

translations.literal: (Records of Unusual Distinctions: The Xuanwu Hall Sons Corps were especially fierce and bold; when their crossbow drew one great mechanism, then twelve small mechanisms all released, using linked-bead great arrows; nothing at a distance was beyond reach, and the men of Jin greatly feared this.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Records of Unusual Distinctions: The Xuanwu Hall Sons Corps were especially fierce. When their crossbow drew one main mechanism, twelve smaller ones fired together, shooting great linked-bead arrows that struck at any range; the men of Jin feared them above all.)]

sentences.zh: 晏球預選，從梁祖征伐，所至立功，累遷廳子都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanqiu was chosen in the selection; he followed the Liang Founder on campaigns, earned merit wherever he went, and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Hall Sons Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu was selected for the corps and followed the Liang Founder on campaign, winning distinction wherever he fought until he rose to command the Hall Sons Corps.

sentences.zh: 梁開平三年，自開封府押衙充直左耀武指揮使，授右千牛衛將軍，軍職如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Liang Kaiping, from Kaifeng Prefecture Escort Officer he served as acting Left Dazzling Martial Commander and was appointed Right Thousand-Ox Guard General, his army post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Liang Kaiping he was made acting commander of the Left Dazzling Martial Guard and Right Thousand-Ox Guard general, while retaining his army command.

sentences.zh: 朱友珪之篡位也，懷州龍驤守禦軍作亂，欲入京城。

translations.literal: When Zhu Yougui usurped the throne, the Huai Prefecture Dragon-Tiger Garrison Defense Army mutinied and wished to enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yougui seized the throne, the Dragon-Tiger garrison at Huai mutinied and tried to march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 已至河陽，友珪命晏球出騎迎戰擊亂軍，獲軍使劉重遇，以功轉左龍驤第一指揮使。

translations.literal: They had already reached Heyang; Yougui ordered Yanqiu to lead cavalry out to meet and strike the mutinous army, captured army commander Liu Chongyu, and for his merit was transferred to First Commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army.
translations.idiomatic: They had reached Heyang when Yougui sent Yanqiu out with cavalry to meet the rebels; he captured the mutiny leader Liu Chongyu and was promoted to first commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝嗣位，以晏球為龍驤四軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Last Liang Emperor succeeded to the throne, he made Yanqiu overall commander of the four Dragon-Tiger armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Liang Emperor took the throne, he made Yanqiu overall commander of the four Dragon-Tiger armies.

sentences.zh: 貞明二年四月十九日夜，汴州捉生都將李霸等作亂，縱火焚剽，攻建國門，梁末帝登樓拒戰。

translations.literal: On the night of the nineteenth day of the fourth month of the second year of Zhenming, Li Ba and others, commanders of the Bianzhou Foraging Corps, mutinied, set fires and looted, attacked the Jianguo Gate, and the Last Liang Emperor mounted the tower to resist.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the nineteenth day of the fourth month of the second year of Zhenming, Li Ba and other commanders of the Bianzhou foraging corps mutinied, setting fires and looting as they attacked the Jianguo Gate; the Last Liang Emperor mounted the tower to fight them off.

sentences.zh: 晏球聞亂，先得龍驤馬五百屯於鞠場，俄而亂兵以竿豎麻布沃油焚建國縷，勢將危急。

translations.literal: Yanqiu heard of the disorder and first gathered five hundred Dragon-Tiger horses and encamped them at the drill ground; soon the mutinous soldiers raised poles with hemp cloth soaked in oil to burn the Jianguo gate tower, and the situation was about to become critical.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the mutiny, Yanqiu first gathered five hundred Dragon-Tiger horses at the drill ground; soon the rebels raised poles draped with oil-soaked cloth to set the Jianguo gate tower ablaze, and the situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 晏球隔門窺亂兵，見無甲胄，即出騎擊之，奮力血戰，俄而群賊散走。

translations.literal: Yanqiu peered through the gate at the mutinous soldiers, saw they wore no armor, and immediately led cavalry out to strike them; fighting fiercely in bloody combat, before long the band of rebels scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu looked through the gate at the rebels, saw they wore no armor, and led his cavalry out to attack; after a fierce fight the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝見騎軍討賊，呼曰：「非吾龍驤之士乎？

translations.literal: The Last Liang Emperor saw the cavalry suppressing the rebels and called out: "Are these not my Dragon-Tiger men?
translations.idiomatic: The Last Liang Emperor saw the cavalry fighting the rebels and called out, "Are those not my Dragon-Tiger men?

sentences.zh: 」晏球奏曰：「亂者惟李霸一都，陛下但守宮城，遲明臣必破之。

translations.literal: " Yanqiu reported: "The mutineers are only Li Ba's one corps; Your Majesty need only hold the palace city, and by dawn your subject will surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanqiu reported, "The rebels are only Li Ba's one corps. Your Majesty need only hold the palace; by dawn I will destroy them.

sentences.zh: 」既而晏球盡戮亂軍，全營族誅，以功授單州刺史。

translations.literal: " Before long Yanqiu slaughtered all the mutinous soldiers and executed the entire camp by clan punishment; for his merit he was appointed prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Yanqiu slaughtered the mutineers and executed their entire camp by clan punishment; for this he was made prefect of Shan.

sentences.zh: 尋領軍於河上，為行營馬軍都指揮兼諸軍排陣使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he led the army on the Yellow River as overall cavalry commander of the campaign headquarters and concurrently array marshal for all armies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took command on the Yellow River as overall cavalry commander of the campaign headquarters and marshal of battle formations for all armies.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，晏球率騎軍入援。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yanqiu led the cavalry army in to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yanqiu led his cavalry in to reinforce the city.

sentences.zh: 至封丘，聞梁末帝殂，即解甲降於莊宗。

translations.literal: When he reached Fengqiu and heard that the Last Liang Emperor had died, he immediately laid down his armor and surrendered to Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengqiu he learned that the Last Liang Emperor was dead and at once laid down his arms and surrendered to Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 明年，與霍彥威北捍契丹，授齊州防禦使、北面行營馬軍都指揮使，仍賜姓氏，名紹虔。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Huo Yanwei he defended the north against the Khitan; he was appointed defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture and cavalry commander of the northern campaign headquarters, and was also granted the imperial surname with the name Shaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined Huo Yanwei in defending the north against the Khitan and was made defense commissioner of Qi and cavalry commander of the northern campaign; he was also granted the imperial surname and the name Shaoqian.

sentences.zh: 鄴之亂，明宗入赴內難，晏球時在瓦橋，遣人招之。

translations.literal: During the disorder at Ye, Emperor Mingzong entered to answer the internal crisis; Yanqiu was then at Waqiao and sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ye mutiny, Emperor Mingzong marched to answer the crisis; Yanqiu was at Waqiao and sent men to summon him.

sentences.zh: 明宗至汴，晏球率騎從至京師，以平定功授宋州節度使，上章求還本姓名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong reached Bian, Yanqiu led cavalry and followed to the capital; for his merit in pacification he was appointed military governor of Song Prefecture and submitted a memorial asking to restore his original surname and given name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong reached Bian, Yanqiu followed with his cavalry to the capital; for his role in the pacification he was made military governor of Song and petitioned to restore his original name.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，授北面行營副招討，以兵戍滿城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was appointed deputy northern pacification commissioner and garrisoned Mancheng with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made deputy northern pacification commissioner and garrisoned Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王都據定州，

translations.literal: That year Wang Du held Ding Prefecture,
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Du held Ding,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：遣人說北面副招討使王晏球，晏球不從，乃以金遺晏球帳下，使圖之，不克。

translations.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: He sent men to persuade the deputy northern pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu; Yanqiu would not follow, so he sent gold to men under Yanqiu's command and had them plot against him, but it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: (Comprehensive Mirror: He sent men to win over the deputy northern pacification commissioner Wang Yanqiu, but Yanqiu refused; he then bribed men in Yanqiu's camp to plot against him, without success.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，晏球以都反狀聞。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Yanqiu reported Du's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Yanqiu reported Du's rebellion to the throne.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以王晏球為北面招討使，權知定州行州事。）〉

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Wang Yanqiu was made northern pacification commissioner and acting administrator of Ding Prefecture affairs.)]
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Wang Yanqiu was made northern pacification commissioner and acting administrator of Ding.)]

sentences.zh: 契丹遣禿餒率騎千餘來援都，突入定州，晏球引軍保曲陽。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Tunei at the head of more than a thousand cavalry to aid Du; they burst into Ding Prefecture, and Yanqiu led his army to hold Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Tunei with more than a thousand cavalry to aid Du; they broke into Ding, and Yanqiu withdrew his army to Quyang.

sentences.zh: 王都、托諾出軍拒戰，晏球督厲軍士，令短兵擊賊，戒之曰：「回首者死。

translations.literal: Wang Du and Tuonuo led troops out to resist; Yanqiu urged and roused his soldiers, ordered close combat against the enemy, and warned them: "Whoever turns back dies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du and Tuonuo marched out to fight; Yanqiu roused his men for close combat and warned them, "Turn back and you die.

sentences.zh: 」符彥卿以龍武左軍攻軍其左，高行周以龍武右軍攻其右，奮劍揮楇，應手首落，賊軍大敗於嘉山之下，追襲至於城門。

translations.literal: " Fu Yanqing with the Left Dragon Martial Army attacked their left, Gao Xingzhou with the Right Dragon Martial Army attacked their right; swinging swords and clubs, heads fell at every blow; the enemy army was greatly defeated below Jia Mountain, and the pursuit reached the city gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Yanqing's Left Dragon Martial Army struck their left flank and Gao Xingzhou's Right Dragon Martial Army their right; swords and clubs flashed and heads fell at every stroke. The enemy was routed below Jia Mountain and pursued to the city gates.

sentences.zh: 俄而契丹首領惕隱率勇騎五千至唐河。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan chieftain Tiyin led five thousand brave cavalry to Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan chieftain Tiyin arrived at Tang River with five thousand elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是時大雨，晏球出師逆戰，惕隱復敗，追至易州，河水暴漲，所在陷沒，俘獲二千騎而還。

translations.literal: At that time there was heavy rain; Yanqiu marched out to meet and fight, Tiyin was again defeated, and the pursuit reached Yi Prefecture; the river waters rose violently and everywhere collapsed and sank; they captured two thousand cavalry and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain was falling when Yanqiu marched out to meet him; Tiyin was defeated again and pursued to Yi, where flooding swallowed men and horses alike; Yanqiu returned with two thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 惕隱以餘眾北走幽州，趙德鈞令牙將武從諫以騎邀擊。

translations.literal: Tiyin fled north to You Prefecture with the remaining force; Zhao Dejun ordered his staff general Wu Congjian to intercept with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Tiyin fled north toward You with the survivors; Zhao Dejun sent his officer Wu Congjian with cavalry to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 德鈞分扼諸要路，旬日之內，盡獲惕隱已下酋長七百餘人，契丹遂弱。

translations.literal: Dejun blocked the key routes in separate detachments; within ten days he captured in full more than seven hundred chieftains from Tiyin downward, and the Khitan were thereby weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun blocked the key routes; within ten days he captured more than seven hundred Khitan chiefs down to Tiyin himself, and Khitan power was broken.

sentences.zh: 晏球圍城既久，帝遣使督攻城，晏球曰：「賊壘堅峻，但食三州租稅，撫恤黎民，愛養軍士彼自當魚潰。

translations.literal: Yanqiu had besieged the city for a long time; the Emperor sent an envoy to urge the assault on the city; Yanqiu said: "The rebel fortifications are strong and steep; if we simply consume the tax grain of three prefectures, soothe and comfort the common people, and cherish and nurture the soldiers, they will collapse of themselves like fish in a net.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege the emperor sent an envoy to urge an assault; Yanqiu said, "The rebel stronghold is formidable. If we simply live off the tax grain of three prefectures, treat the people well, and care for our soldiers, the enemy will collapse on their own.

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 晏珠能與將士同其甘苦，所得祿賜私財，盡以饗士，日具飲饌，與將校筵宴，待軍士有禮，軍中無不敬伏。

translations.literal: Yanzhu was able to share hardship and ease with officers and soldiers; all salary, rewards, and private wealth he obtained he used entirely to feast the troops; daily he prepared food and drink and held banquets with commanders; he treated the soldiers with courtesy, and in the army none failed to respect and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu shared hardship and comfort with his officers and men, spending every stipend and private coin on feasts for the troops; he dined daily with his commanders and treated the rank and file with courtesy, winning the respect of the entire army.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，平賊。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels were subdued.

sentences.zh: 自初戰至於城拔，不戮一士，上下歡心，物議以為有將帥之略，以功授天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: From the first battle until the city was taken, not one soldier was executed; above and below were pleased at heart; public opinion held that he possessed the strategy of a commander; for his merit he was appointed military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: From the first battle until the city fell he did not execute a single soldier; officers and men alike were content, and opinion held that he had a commander's true gift; for this he was made military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮青州，就加兼中書令。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to garrison Qing Prefecture and was concurrently promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Qing and concurrently promoted to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長興三年，卒於鎮，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing he died at his post, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing he died at his post, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 子徹，位至懷州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Che rose to the post of prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che rose to prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 戴思遠，本梁之故將也。

translations.literal: Dai Siyuan was originally an old general of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan had been a general of Liang.

sentences.zh: 初事梁祖，以武幹知名。

translations.literal: He first served the Liang Founder and was known for martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Liang Founder and was known for his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 開平元年，自右羽林統軍加檢校司徒，出為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping, from Right Forest Guard Commander he was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Education and sent out as prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiping he was made acting Minister of Education and sent out as prefect of Jin, having served as commander of the Right Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，授右監門上將軍，尋改華州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Right Gate Guard Senior General and soon changed to defense commissioner of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made senior general of the Right Gate Guard, then defense commissioner of Hua.

sentences.zh: 三年，自左天武使復授右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, from Left Heavenly Martial Commander he was again appointed Right Forest Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to command the Right Forest Guard after serving as commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 郢王友珪篡位，授洺州團練使。

translations.literal: When Prince Ying Yougui usurped the throne, he was appointed training commissioner of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ying Yougui usurped the throne, he was made training commissioner of Ming.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，為邢州留後，遷本州節度使。

translations.literal: During Zhenming he served as regent of Xing Prefecture and was transferred to military governor of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenming he was regent of Xing and then military governor of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬燕將張萬進殺滄州留後劉繼威，以城歸梁，末帝命思遠鎮之。

translations.literal: When the Yan general Zhang Wanjin killed Cang Prefecture regent Liu Jiwei and surrendered the city to Liang, the Last Emperor ordered Siyuan to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan general Zhang Wanjin killed the regent of Cang, Liu Jiwei, and surrendered the city to Liang, the Last Emperor sent Siyuan to take command there.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定魏博，以兵臨滄、德，思遠棄鎮渡河歸汴，累遷天平軍節度使兼北面招討使，將兵與莊宗對壘。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Weibo and pressed Cang and De with troops, Siyuan abandoned his post, crossed the river, and returned to Bian; he was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Tianping Army and concurrent northern pacification commissioner, leading troops to face Emperor Zhuangzong in camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Weibo and marched on Cang and De, Siyuan abandoned his post, crossed the river, and fled to Bian; he rose to military governor of Tianping and northern pacification commissioner and led troops to face Emperor Zhuangzong in the field.

sentences.zh: 久之，莊宗討張文禮於鎮州，契丹來援，莊宗追襲契丹至幽州。

translations.literal: After a long time Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture; the Khitan came to aid him, and Emperor Zhuangzong pursued and struck the Khitan as far as You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Zhuangzong marched against Zhang Wenli at Zhen; when the Khitan came to his aid, Emperor Zhuangzong pursued them all the way to You.

sentences.zh: 思遠聞之，總兵以襲魏州，至魏店，遇明宗騎軍適至，思遠乃涉洹水，陷成安，復歸楊村寨，盡率其眾，攻德勝北城。

translations.literal: When Siyuan heard of this, he gathered troops to strike Wei Prefecture; reaching Weidian, he happened upon Emperor Mingzong's cavalry arriving; Siyuan then crossed the Huan River, took Chengan, returned to Yangjia Village, led out his entire force, and attacked the north city of Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Siyuan massed troops to strike Wei; at Weidian he ran into Emperor Mingzong's cavalry arriving, so he crossed the Huan River, took Chengan, withdrew to Yangjia Village, and led his full force against the north city of Desheng.

sentences.zh: 城中危急，符存審晝夜乘城以拒之。

translations.literal: The city was in grave peril; Fu Cunshen day and night mounted the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The city was in dire straits; Fu Cunshen mounted the walls day and night to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 莊宗自薊五日馳至魏州，思遠聞之解去。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong galloped from Ji to Wei Prefecture in five days; when Siyuan heard of it he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong rode from Ji to Wei in five days; on hearing of his approach Siyuan broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及明宗襲下鄆州，思遠罷軍權，降授宣化軍留後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong stormed and took Yan Prefecture, Siyuan was stripped of military authority and demoted to regent of the Xuanhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong captured Yan, Siyuan lost his military command and was demoted to regent of Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 其年，莊宗入汴，思遠自鄧州入朝，復令歸鎮。

translations.literal: That year, when Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Siyuan came to court from Deng Prefecture and was again ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Siyuan came to court from Deng and was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，移授洋州節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was transferred and appointed military governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was transferred to military governor of Yang.

sentences.zh: 及西川俱叛，思遠以董璋故人，避嫌請代，征入朝宿衛，以年告老，授太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: When both parts of the West Riverland rebelled, Siyuan, being an old acquaintance of Dong Zhang, sought to avoid suspicion and asked to be replaced; he was summoned to court for palace guard duty, reported his age and retired, and was appointed Crown Prince Junior Mentor with retirement honors.
translations.idiomatic: When both Shu territories rebelled, Siyuan, an old friend of Dong Zhang, asked to be replaced to avoid suspicion; he was recalled to court for palace guard duty, then retired on grounds of age as Crown Prince Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年八月，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Qingtai he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Qingtai he died at home.

sentences.zh: 朱漢賓，字績臣，亳州譙縣人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Hanbin, whose courtesy name was Jichen, was a native of Qiao County in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hanbin, courtesy name Jichen, came from Qiao County in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父元禮，始為郡將。

translations.literal: His father Yuanli originally served as a prefectural commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanli had begun as a prefectural commander.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖聞其名，擢為軍校，從龐師古渡淮，戰沒於淮南。

translations.literal: The Liang Founder heard his name and promoted him to army officer; following Pang Shigu in crossing the Huai, he died in battle south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Founder heard of him and made him an army officer; he followed Pang Shigu across the Huai and was killed in battle in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 漢賓少有膂力，形神壯偉，膽氣過人。

translations.literal: Hanbin in youth had great physical strength; his form and spirit were robust and imposing, and his courage surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hanbin was immensely strong, with an imposing build and courage beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 梁祖以其父死王事，選置帳下，編入屬籍。

translations.literal: Because his father had died in the ruler's service, the Liang Founder selected him and placed him under his command, enrolling him in the roster of followers.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in imperial service, the Liang Founder took him into his personal retinue and enrolled him among his followers.

sentences.zh: 梁祖之攻兗、鄆也，朱瑾募驍勇數百人，黥雙雁於其頰，立為「雁子都」。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder attacked Yan and Yun, Zhu Jin recruited several hundred fierce warriors, tattooed twin geese on their cheeks, and established them as the "Goose Sons Corps."
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder attacked Yan and Yun, Zhu Jin recruited several hundred fierce warriors, tattooed twin geese on their cheeks, and formed them into the "Goose Sons Corps."

sentences.zh: 梁祖聞之，亦選數百人，別為一軍，號為「落雁都」。

translations.literal: When the Liang Founder heard of this, he too selected several hundred men, formed them into a separate army, and called it the "Falling Geese Corps."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, the Liang Founder selected several hundred men of his own, formed a separate corps, and called it the "Falling Geese Corps."

sentences.zh: 署漢賓為軍使，當時目為「朱落雁」。

translations.literal: He appointed Hanbin as corps commander; at the time he was known as "Zhu the Falling Goose."
translations.idiomatic: He made Hanbin corps commander, and at the time people called him "Zhu the Falling Goose."

sentences.zh: 後與諸將破蔡賊有功，天復中，授右羽林統軍。

translations.literal: Later, together with the other generals he had merit in defeating the Cai bandits; during Tianfu he was appointed Right Forest Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later he helped the other generals defeat the Cai bandits; during Tianfu he was made commander of the Right Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 入梁，曆天威軍使、左羽林統軍，出為磁州刺史、滑宋二州留後、亳曹二州刺史、安州節度使。

translations.literal: After entering Liang he served successively as Heavenly Might Army commander and Left Forest Guard Commander, and was sent out as prefect of Ci Prefecture, regent of Hua and Song, prefect of Bo and Cao, and military governor of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as commander of the Heavenly Might Army and the Left Forest Guard, then as prefect of Ci, regent of Hua and Song, prefect of Bo and Cao, and military governor of An.

sentences.zh: 莊宗至洛陽，漢賓自鎮入覲，復令還鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong reached Luoyang, Hanbin came from his post to audience and was again ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong reached Luoyang, Hanbin came from his post for an audience and was sent back.

sentences.zh: 明年，授左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Left Dragon Martial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嘗幸漢賓之第，漢賓妻進酒上食，奏家樂以娛之，自是漢賓頗蒙寵待。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong once visited Hanbin's residence; Hanbin's wife presented wine and served food and played household music to entertain him; from then on Hanbin received considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong once visited Hanbin at home; Hanbin's wife served wine and food and played household music for him, and from then on Hanbin enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 同光四年正月，冀王朱友謙入朝，明宗居洛陽，以友謙故人，置酒於第。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Tongguang, Prince Ji Zhu Youqian came to court; Emperor Mingzong was in Luoyang and, being an old friend of Youqian, set out wine at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Tongguang, Prince Ji Zhu Youqian came to court; Emperor Mingzong was in Luoyang and, as an old friend of Youqian, held a banquet at his residence.

sentences.zh: 莊宗諸弟在席，友謙坐在永王存霸之上。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brothers were at the table; Youqian was seated above Prince Yong Cunba.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brothers were present; Youqian was seated above Prince Yong Cunba.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，漢賓以大觴奉友謙曰：「公雖名位高，坐於皇弟之上，非宜也。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Hanbin offered Youqian a great cup and said: "Sir, though your fame and rank are high, to sit above the emperor's brothers is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Hanbin raised a great cup to Youqian and said, "Sir, though your rank is high, it is not fitting to sit above the emperor's brothers.

sentences.zh: 仆與公俱在梁朝，以宗盟相厚，自公入朝，三發單函候問，略無報復，忽餘卑位，不亦甚乎！

translations.literal: I and you were both in the house of Liang and were close as clansmen; since you entered court I have sent three separate letters of inquiry, with scarcely any reply; suddenly to treat me as beneath you—is this not excessive!
translations.idiomatic: You and I were both in Liang and bound by clan ties; since you came to court I have sent three letters of inquiry with scarcely a reply. To treat me as beneath you—is that not going too far!

sentences.zh: 」元行欽恐其紛然，為解之方止。

translations.literal: " Yuan Xingqin feared a quarrel would break out and mediated to settle it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Xingqin, fearing a quarrel, stepped in to smooth things over.

sentences.zh: 不數日，友謙赤族。

translations.literal: Within a few days Youqian's entire clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Youqian's entire clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮據魏州，元行欽率軍進討，詔漢賓權知河南府事。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili held Wei Prefecture, Yuan Xingqin led the army forward to suppress him; an edict made Hanbin acting administrator of Henan Prefecture affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili held Wei, Yuan Xingqin marched to suppress him; Hanbin was made acting administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 明宗以漢賓為右衛上將軍，樞密使安重誨方當委重，漢賓密令結托，得為婚家。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong made Hanbin Right Guard Senior General; the Palace Commissioner An Chonghui was then in full trust, and Hanbin secretly had connections made and became related by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong made Hanbin senior general of the Right Guard; Palace Commissioner An Chonghui was then at the height of power, and Hanbin cultivated ties with him until their families were joined by marriage.

sentences.zh: 天成末，為潞州節度使，移鎮晉州。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiancheng he was military governor of Lu Prefecture and was transferred to garrison Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tiancheng he was military governor of Lu, then was transferred to Jin.

sentences.zh: 重誨既誅，漢賓復為上將軍。

translations.literal: After Chonghui was executed, Hanbin again became senior general.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghui was executed, Hanbin returned to the post of senior general.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，漢賓告老，授太子少保致仕。

translations.literal: The next autumn Hanbin reported his age and retired; he was appointed Crown Prince Junior Mentor with retirement honors.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn Hanbin retired on grounds of age and was made Crown Prince Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年六月卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of the second year of Qingtai, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the second year of Qingtai, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子四人，長曰崇勳，官至左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He had four sons; the eldest was named Chongxun, who rose to Left Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; the eldest, Chongxun, rose to general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 有子師道，仕皇朝，為右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: He had a son Shidao, who served the Imperial Dynasty as Right Advisor-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Shidao who served our dynasty as Right Advisor-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 周知裕，字好問，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiyu, whose courtesy name was Haowen, was a native of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiyu, courtesy name Haowen, came from You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少事燕帥劉仁恭為騎將，表為媯州刺史。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Yan commander Liu Rengong as a cavalry officer and was memorialized as prefect of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served the Yan commander Liu Rengong as a cavalry officer and was recommended as prefect of Gui.

sentences.zh: 久之，移刺德州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to serve as prefect of De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to prefect of De.

sentences.zh: 天祐四年，劉守光既平滄州，乃以其幼子繼威為留後，大將張萬進與知裕佐之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianyou, after Liu Shouguang had pacified Cang Prefecture, he made his youngest son Jiwei regent, with the great general Zhang Wanjin and Zhiyu to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianyou, after Liu Shouguang pacified Cang, he made his youngest son Jiwei regent, with the great general Zhang Wanjin and Zhiyu to assist him.

sentences.zh: 繼威衝幼，宣淫於萬進之家，萬進殺之。

translations.literal: Jiwei was young and rash; he openly debauched himself in Wanjin's household, and Wanjin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwei was young and headstrong and openly debauched himself in Wanjin's household; Wanjin killed him.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，召知裕告其故，萬進自稱留後，署知裕為景州刺史。

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned Zhiyu and told him the reason; Wanjin declared himself regent and appointed Zhiyu prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he summoned Zhiyu and explained what he had done; Wanjin declared himself regent and appointed Zhiyu prefect of Jing.

sentences.zh: 會萬進納款於梁，知裕先奔於汴，梁主厚待之。

translations.literal: When Wanjin submitted to Liang, Zhiyu fled first to Bian; the Liang ruler treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanjin submitted to Liang, Zhiyu fled first to Bian, where the Liang ruler received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 特置歸化軍，以知裕為指揮使。

translations.literal: A Return-to-Grace Army was specially established, with Zhiyu as its commander.
translations.idiomatic: A special Return-to-Grace Army was created with Zhiyu as its commander.

sentences.zh: 凡軍士自河朔歸梁者，皆隸於部下。

translations.literal: All soldiers who returned to Liang from the Hebei region were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: All soldiers who came over to Liang from the Hebei region were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 梁與莊宗交戰於河，摧堅挫銳，惟恃歸化一軍，然歲將一紀，位不及郡守。

translations.literal: When Liang and Emperor Zhuangzong fought on the river, breaking hardened foes and blunting sharp attacks, they relied solely on the Return-to-Grace Army; yet nearly a full cycle of years passed and his rank did not reach that of a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's battles with Emperor Zhuangzong on the Yellow River, where hardened lines were broken and elite troops blunted, they relied solely on the Return-to-Grace Army; yet after nearly twelve years his rank still fell short of a prefect.

sentences.zh: 同光初，莊宗入汴，知裕隨段凝軍解甲封丘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, when Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhiyu followed Duan Ning's army in laying down arms at Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang, when Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhiyu followed Duan Ning's army in surrendering at Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 明宗時為總管，受降於郊外，見知裕甚喜，遙相謂曰：「周歸化今為吾人，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong was then overall commander and received the surrender in the suburbs; seeing Zhiyu he was greatly pleased and called out from afar: "Zhou of the Return-to-Grace Army is now one of ours—what joy could equal this!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong was then overall commander and received the surrender outside the city; seeing Zhiyu he was delighted and called out from afar, "Zhou of the Return-to-Grace Army is ours now—what could bring greater joy!

sentences.zh: 」因令諸子以兄事之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered his sons to treat him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: " He then told his sons to treat Zhiyu as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 莊宗撫憐尤異，而諸校心妒之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong showed him special favor and affection, but the various officers resented him in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong showed him exceptional favor, but the other officers grew jealous.

sentences.zh: 有壯士唐從益者，因獵射之，知裕遁而獲免。

translations.literal: There was a strong man named Tang Congyi who, while hunting, shot at him; Zhiyu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A warrior named Tang Congyi shot at him while hunting; Zhiyu fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遂誅從益，出知裕為房州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong then executed Congyi and sent Zhiyu out as prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong executed Congyi and sent Zhiyu out as prefect of Fang.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌伐蜀，召為前鋒騎將。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu, he was summoned as vanguard cavalry commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu, he was summoned as vanguard cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，移刺絳州，改淄州刺史、宿州團練使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Jiang Prefecture, then changed to prefect of Zi Prefecture and training commissioner of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he was transferred to Jiang, then made prefect of Zi and training commissioner of Su.

sentences.zh: 知裕老於軍旅，勤於稼穡，凡為郡勸課，皆有政聲，朝廷喜之，遷安州留後。

translations.literal: Zhiyu was seasoned in military affairs and diligent in farming; wherever he governed a prefecture and urged cultivation, he had a reputation for good administration; the court was pleased and transferred him to regent of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu was a veteran of camp and field and diligent in promoting agriculture; in every prefecture he governed he won a reputation for good administration, and the court was pleased to make him regent of An.

sentences.zh: 淮上之風惡病者，至於父母有疾，不親省視，甚者避於他室；

translations.literal: The custom along the Huai feared the sick; when parents fell ill they would not personally visit and attend them, and in extreme cases they avoided them in another room;
translations.idiomatic: Along the Huai there was a custom of shunning the sick; when parents fell ill their children would not visit them in person, and some even kept to another room;

sentences.zh: 或時問訊，即以食物揭於長竿之首，委之而去。

translations.literal: when they occasionally inquired after them, they would attach food to the end of a long pole, leave it, and go away.
translations.idiomatic: when they did inquire, they would tie food to the end of a long pole, leave it, and go away.

sentences.zh: 知裕心惡之，召鄉之頑很者訶詰教導，俾知父子骨肉之恩，由是弊風稍革。

translations.literal: Zhiyu detested this in his heart; he summoned the stubborn and harsh men of the district, rebuked and instructed them, and made them understand the bond of father and son and flesh and bone; thereby the corrupt custom was gradually reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu abhorred this practice; he summoned the most stubborn men of the district, rebuked and instructed them in the bonds of family, and gradually reformed the custom.

sentences.zh: 長興末，入為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing he entered court as Right Divine Martial Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changxing he was recalled to court as commander of the Right Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，卒於官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫才之良者，在秦亦良也，在虞亦良也。

translations.literal: The historian says: A man of fine talent is fine in Qin and fine in Yu as well.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: True talent shines wherever it serves—in Qin or in Yu alike.

sentences.zh: 故彥威而下，昔為梁臣，不虧亮節；

translations.literal: Thus from Yanwei downward, though they were once ministers of Liang, they did not compromise their bright integrity;
translations.idiomatic: From Yanwei downward, though they had once served Liang, they never compromised their integrity;

sentences.zh: 洎歸唐祚，亦無醜聲，蓋鬆貞不變於四時，玉粹寧虞其烈焰故也。

translations.literal: and when they returned to the fortune of Tang they likewise had no disgraceful reputation—for the pine keeps its constancy through the four seasons, and pure jade need not fear blazing fire.
translations.idiomatic: and when they entered Tang's service they bore no stain on their names—for the pine keeps its constancy through every season, and pure jade does not fear the flame.

sentences.zh: 況彥威之輔明宗也，有翊戴之績；

translations.literal: Moreover, in aiding Emperor Mingzong, Yanwei had the achievement of supporting his accession;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yanwei had the achievement of supporting Emperor Mingzong's accession;

sentences.zh: 晏球之伐中山也，著戡定之功。

translations.literal: and in campaigning against Zhongshan, Yanqiu displayed the merit of pacification and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: and Yanqiu won distinction in pacifying Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 方之數公，尤為優矣。

translations.literal: Compared with the several others, they were especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Among these men, they stood out above the rest.
